newsitem.title: USA: U.S. prepared to join Bosnia force - Solana.
newsitem.headline: U.S. prepared to join Bosnia force - Solana.

text.p: The Clinton administration has told NATO it is preparing to take part in a new international military force of up to 30,000 troops in Bosnia next year, NATO Secretary General Javier Solana said on Thursday.

"Yes. Leave it at that," Solana told reporters when asked if he had been given a positive signal by U.S. Vice President Al Gore in a White House meeting on Wednesday. Solana said the United States might send as many as 7,000 to 8,000 troops to Bosnia as part of the new force.

"I have the impression that the final (U.S.) position will be taken in the coming hours, and the position to my mind will be a positive response to continue," Solana said at a breakfast with defence writers. He said he hoped the new force would be out of Bosnia by the end of next year.

President Bill Clinton was to meet with his national security advisers later in the day and the Washington Post reported that he could make an announcement on Bosnia participation before leaving on Friday for a vacation in Hawaii.

Solana said that he expected formal approval for the new force by NATO political leaders in Brussels next Monday and that he expected the force, which would replace a current NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) of 50,000, would total "about 25,000 on the ground -- between 20,000 and 30,000."

The United States is currently beginning to pull its 15,000-member IFOR contingent out of Bosnia and Solana said he expected that Washington could provide "7,000 or 8,000 troops" to the post-IFOR force.
